~Is Koh Samui safe for tourists? | Yes, generally. Violent crime against visitors is rare; the real risks are scooter crashes, rip currents and box jellyfish in the sea, and alcohol-related trouble on party nights. A helmet, respect for red flags and a pre-booked ride home cover most of it.
Is Koh Samui safe for solo female travellers? | Many women travel alone on Samui without problems. Use Grab or a registered taxi at night rather than walking dark roads or beaches, watch your drink, share your location with a friend and choose accommodation with staffed reception. Call 1155 or 191 if anything happens.
Is Koh Samui safe at night? | The busy parts of Chaweng, Lamai and Fisherman's Village are lively and well lit until late. The main night-time risks are riding a scooter after drinking, unlit roads and loose dogs, spiked drinks and swimming in the dark, so take a taxi home and stay out of the sea.
Is it safe to drink tap water on Koh Samui? | No. Drink bottled or filtered water, which is cheap and sold everywhere, and use refill stations where your hotel has them. Brushing your teeth with tap water is fine for most people.
Are there dangerous animals on Koh Samui? | The ones to respect are box jellyfish in the sea, loose dogs (rabies is present in Thailand, so any bite needs hospital the same day), mosquitoes that carry dengue, and occasional snakes and centipedes in gardens.
Is it safe to go to the Full Moon Party from Samui? | Yes, if you plan it. Book a licensed return boat before you go, watch your drinks, stay with friends and don't buy drugs. Our shared Full Moon Party speedboat costs 1,400 THB return with hotel pickup from most areas of Koh Samui.
What are the emergency numbers in Thailand? | 1155 for the English-speaking Tourist Police, 191 for the police, 1669 for an ambulance and 199 for fire. On Samui, Bangkok Hospital Samui also has a local hotline on 1719.
Is Koh Samui safe in the rainy season? | Yes, with care. From October to December, and especially in November, expect heavy rain, flooded low roads, rough seas and red flags on Chaweng and Lamai. Avoid riding in downpours, don't swim on red-flag days and allow a buffer day before flights in case boats stop.
Can I get arrested for vaping in Thailand? | Yes. Vapes and e-cigarettes are illegal to bring in, possess or use, and there are no exceptions for tourists. Visitors have been fined and detained, so leave them at home.
What should I do if my passport is stolen on Samui? | Report it to the Tourist Police on 1155 or the local police station and get a written report, then contact your embassy in Bangkok for an emergency travel document. Koh Samui Immigration in Maenam can transfer your permitted stay to the new document.
